record.paper_title: Recent developments and open problems in linear series
record.original_question: Let X be the blow-up of P^2 at r general points, let D be an effective divisor on X, and let E be a (-1)-curve. For the restriction map from the complete linear system |D| to |D|_E|, must all base points in the image come from a fixed base curve of |D|, and, if |D| has no fixed component, must the restriction map have maximal rank?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.9.3 Let X be the blow-up of P2 in r general points, D an effective divisor on X and E a (−1)-curve. For the restriction map |D| ρ→ |D|E| one has: 1. All base points in the image of ρ come from a base curve in |D|. 2. If |D| has no fixed component, then ρ has maximal rank.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be the blow-up of the projective plane $\mathbb{P}^2$ at $r$ general points, let $D$ be an effective divisor on $X$, and let $E \subset X$ be a $(-1)$-curve (a smooth rational curve with self-intersection $-1$). Consider the complete linear system $|D|$ on $X$ and the restriction map
$$\rho \colon |D| \longrightarrow |D|_E|,$$
where $|D|_E|$ denotes the linear system on $E$ cut out by $|D|$. Prove or disprove the following two statements:

(1) Every base point of the image linear system $\rho(|D|) \subseteq |D|_E|$ on $E$ arises from a fixed base curve of $|D|$ on $X$ (i.e., it is the image on $E$ of a base curve component of $|D|$).

(2) If $|D|$ has no fixed component, then $\rho$ has maximal rank, meaning that $\rho$ is either injective or surjective as a linear map of vector spaces.
artifact.category_tag: linear systems on blow-ups of P^2
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture is part of the circle of problems around the SHGH conjecture on linear systems on blow-ups of $\mathbb{P}^2$ at general points. No proof of this restriction-map statement (in full generality, for arbitrary effective $D$ and $(-1)$-curves $E$) appears in the literature; it is stated as a conjecture in surveys on linear series and remains open as far as accessible sources indicate.
